paragraphs.claim: The team frames a five-year, two-asset trading task without giving any result.
paragraphs.support: Three present-tense sentences; no measured quantity in the paragraph.
paragraphs.author_qualifier: Source-authored claim or official-task paraphrase; no independent model rerun.
paragraphs.consequence: The reader knows the scope before any number appears.
paragraphs.next_link: The next paragraph answers the first request and ends with the terminal value.

paragraphs.claim: The first request is answered as a sequence ending in one dollar figure.
paragraphs.support: Ordinal markers carry the sequence; the dollar figure and date close the paragraph.
paragraphs.author_qualifier: Source-authored claim or official-task paraphrase; no independent model rerun.
paragraphs.consequence: The terminal value is visible in the summary, unlike a paper that withholds it.
paragraphs.next_link: The next paragraph answers the second request with three criteria.

paragraphs.claim: The second request is answered by generalization, robustness and yield.
paragraphs.support: By, Furthermore and Finally mark the three criteria; respectively closes the value list.
paragraphs.author_qualifier: Source-authored claim or official-task paraphrase; no independent model rerun.
paragraphs.consequence: Three trader outcomes are on record before the body proves them.
paragraphs.next_link: The next paragraph answers the third request.

paragraphs.claim: The third request is answered by a definition, two reported sensitivities, and a comparison.
paragraphs.support: The comparison is attributed to a comparison rather than derived in prose.
paragraphs.author_qualifier: Source-authored claim or official-task paraphrase; no independent model rerun.
paragraphs.consequence: The reader gets the comparison before the sensitivity section.
paragraphs.next_link: The next paragraph only names the fourth deliverable.

paragraphs.dominant_move: name the deliverable, give no new number
paragraphs.claim: The fourth request is answered by naming the memorandum and nothing else.
paragraphs.support: One sentence across three printed lines; no new quantity.
paragraphs.author_qualifier: Source-authored claim or official-task paraphrase; no independent model rerun.
paragraphs.consequence: The summary closes on the form of the answer, not on a result.
paragraphs.next_link: The summary ends; the background section starts the body.

paragraphs.dominant_move: asset > source > figure > second asset > source
paragraphs.claim: Two assets and two sources establish the data the models will use.
paragraphs.support: One source sentence per asset; the figure sits mid-paragraph.

global_organization_chain: Summary: scope with no numbers, then one paragraph per official deliverable, terminal value inside the first (p1).
Background: two assets, two sources, one figure (p3).
Restatement: past-only horizon, then four single-request bullets with no method (p3).
Analysis: a reason before each choice, one choice per request (pp3-4).
Assumptions and notation: purpose, one restriction per bullet, symbols in a table (p5).
Preprocessing: usability rule, calendar gap, per-period rescaling (p6).
Model: cited baseline, components with formulas, paired coefficients, comparative trading rule (pp6-9).
Solving: cost to avoid, guarded action, constraints in order (pp11-12).
Results: parameters, terminal value, repeated coefficient pair, deposit benchmark (pp12-13, p17).
Best-strategy evidence: three criteria, one trader type per paragraph, table, perturbation claim (pp14-17).
Sensitivity: definition after the scenario, one factor at a time, figure reading, comparison (pp18-19).
Limitations: one named gap, one broader gap (p20).
Memorandum: four-line header, direct address, three questions, restated route (pp20-22).

section_progressions.positive_pattern: scope > one deliverable per paragraph > terminal number inside the first deliverable
moves: input: official four requests, two tradable assets, a five-year window
rhetorical job: Open with scope only, then give one paragraph to each official deliverable, ending the second paragraph with the terminal dollar figure.
analytical job: Put the forecast before the plan, and put the plan before the reported value.
output: Five summary paragraphs, the second of which states the terminal dollar figure.
handoff: 1.1 Problem Background.

section_progressions.positive_pattern: asset > source > figure > second asset > source
moves: input: the two named assets and their public price files
rhetorical job: Name each asset, attach one source sentence, and point at a figure in the middle of the paragraph.
analytical job: Place the data the later models will consume.
output: One background paragraph with a figure reference.
handoff: 1.2 Restatement of the Problem.

section_progressions.positive_pattern: information limit > one bullet per deliverable > no method yet
moves: input: the official 2022 C task
rhetorical job: State the information horizon once, then give each request its own bullet with no method attached.
analytical job: Fix the portfolio notation and the past-only rule before any model appears.
output: One horizon sentence plus four single-request bullets.
handoff: 1.3 Problem Analysis.

section_progressions.positive_pattern: reason > choice, repeated once per request
moves: input: the four restated requests
rhetorical job: Give a reason before each choice: forecast before planning, a model chosen for what it does not need, a guess then a measure, three named criteria, an intuition then a reused model.
analytical job: Assign ARIMA to the forecast, a variance proxy to risk, and the first-question model to the cost test.
output: A method plan for all four requests.
handoff: 2.1 Assumptions.

section_progressions.positive_pattern: purpose > one restriction per bullet > reason before restriction
moves: input: the method plan
rhetorical job: State a purpose, then list one assumption per bullet, with the reason in front of the restriction where a reason is given.
analytical job: Fix data trust, trader circumstances, and the ignored minimum trade size.
output: A purpose sentence and a short assumption list.
handoff: 2.2 Notations.

section_progressions.positive_pattern: main symbols in a table > the rest at first use
moves: input: the symbols the later formulas will use
rhetorical job: Point the main symbols to a table and promise the rest at first use.
analytical job: Separate tabulated symbols from locally defined ones.
output: A two-sentence pointer to Table 1.
handoff: 3.1 Data Preprocessing.

section_progressions.positive_pattern: usability rule > observed gap > reason > rescaling
moves: input: the two price files and the period-based plan
rhetorical job: State the usability rule first, then the calendar gap and its fill, then the reason for standardizing by period.
analytical job: Align the two calendars and rescale each period before fitting.
output: A rule sentence, a fill step, and a per-period standardization.
handoff: 3.2.1 Price Prediction Model.

section_progressions.positive_pattern: cited baseline > name, role, order, formula > paired report > comparative rule
moves: input: standardized period data and the past-only rule
rhetorical job: Cite the model as widely used, split it into named components each followed by its formula, report the two fitted coefficients as a pair, then state the decision rule as a comparison.
analytical job: Build ARIMA(p,d,q), report both coefficients, and attach the decision coefficient to the trade rule.
output: Component formulas, one reported coefficient pair, and a threshold trading rule.
handoff: 3.3 Model Solving.

section_progressions.positive_pattern: cost to avoid > guarded action > constraints in order > comparison
moves: input: the threshold trading rule and the five constraints
rhetorical job: Name the cost to be avoided before the action, walk the constraints in printed order, then use a comparison to justify raising the buy share.
analytical job: Restrict trades to threshold crossings with enough cash held back, and tie the decision coefficient to the buy share.
output: A guarded trading procedure and a coefficient-to-share rule.
handoff: 3.4.1 Model Results.

section_progressions.positive_pattern: parameters > terminal value > repeated pair > benchmark > contrast
moves: input: the guarded trading procedure
rhetorical job: State the parameter set, then the terminal value and trade count; repeat the coefficient pair as the evaluation; set a deposit benchmark and contrast the three strategies with it.
analytical job: Report one terminal value, reuse the same coefficient pair as evidence, and compare against a deposit after inflation.
output: A terminal value, a repeated coefficient pair, and a deposit comparison.
handoff: 4 Problem 2, then the memorandum.

section_progressions.positive_pattern: criteria > one actor per paragraph > table reading > two-step definition > claim
moves: input: the three criteria named in the analysis
rhetorical job: Restate the three criteria, give each trader type its own purpose and means, read the comparison table, then rewrite robustness twice before claiming the result.
analytical job: Map three trader types onto the parameter columns and test the rule under perturbation.
output: Three trader profiles, a table reading, and a perturbation claim.
handoff: 4.3 Yield.

section_progressions.positive_pattern: scenario > definition > one factor at a time > one observation per sentence > comparison
moves: input: the cost parameters of the trading rule
rhetorical job: Define the measure after the scenario, change one rate at a time, then read the figure one observation per sentence and end with a comparison.
analytical job: Perturb each commission separately and compare the two sensitivities.
output: A sensitivity definition, four single-factor cases, and one comparison.
handoff: 6.2 Possible Improvements.

section_progressions.positive_pattern: named gap > needed repair > broader gap left unnamed
moves: input: the finished strategy and its reported checks
rhetorical job: Name one concrete gap and the repair it needs, then a broader gap with no formula attached.
analytical job: Mark the untreated mixed-purchase case and the missing domain knowledge.
output: Two stated gaps.
handoff: 7 Memorandum.

section_progressions.positive_pattern: header > direct address > three questions > restated route > restated numbers
moves: input: the four answered requests and the trader recipient
rhetorical job: Open with a four-line header, address the reader directly, reduce the strategy to three questions, then restate the model choice and the coefficient pair.
analytical job: Carry the route, the reported numbers, and the symbol definitions to the recipient.
output: A dated memorandum of about two pages.
handoff: End of the submitted solution; references and appendix are evidence only.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The prose says the decision coefficient is better when closer to 1, and it treats the risk term as a measured penalty.
warnings.warning: Equation (3) is a ratio of residual sums of squares, so closer to 1 means a worse fit, the opposite of the sentence. Equation (5) sums a term that does not depend on its index, so the risk term is identically zero as printed. The skill must keep both the sentence and the formula and must not teach either as a working definition.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The objective penalizes risk through S_j over a 30-day window.
warnings.warning: The left side carries subscript j and the right side never uses j. Rewriting the summand as A_j would invent a formula the page does not print. As printed the penalty vanishes and the objective collapses to raw assets.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The strategy uses only prices known on the day of the trade.
warnings.warning: The gold sale in equation (6) settles at Y_{g(i+1)}, the next period's price, and equations (14) to (16) divide the gold purchase by the next period's realized price. The bitcoin sale condition subtracts X at i-1 rather than i. A past-only claim cannot be copied from these lines.
warnings.cross_model_note: The printed warning also cites equations owned by another model; the audit entry keeps only this model's equations so the owner check holds.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The bitcoin holding updates on its own symbol.
warnings.warning: Both branches of the unnumbered bitcoin update start from G_{i-1}. The page prints G, so substituting B would fix a defect the authors printed. The skill must not execute this line as a bitcoin update.

warnings.precise_source_claim: Three labelled cases cover a high purchase, a low purchase and a sale.
warnings.warning: The case labelled with the high gold weight computes with the low one, the low label computes with the high one, and the sale label computes a purchase. All three leave bitcoin unchanged. Following the labels and following the formulas give different trades.

warnings.precise_source_claim: The deposit is worth $139.2436 after five years, so trading beats cash.
warnings.warning: Equation (17) prints the factor as an exponent. With the printed inputs the exponent reading gives about 397 and ordinary compounding gives about 714. Neither is the reported 139.2436. The comparison with the trading result rests on a number the printed formula does not produce.

warnings.precise_source_claim: Sensitivity is defined as the change rate of transaction frequency.
warnings.warning: Equation (18) has no left side and no equals sign, and the section heading prints Difinition. The expression cannot be cited as a definition without adding a symbol the page does not print.

warnings.precise_source_claim: Figure 6 draws the same trading test as equation (6).
warnings.warning: The diamonds print X_{g(i+1)} minus Y_{gi}, then |X_g - Y_g|, three different subscripts on one chart, none of them the g(i) and g(i-1) of equation (6). The chart and the equation are not the same test. Copying either as the rule drops the other.
warnings.cross_model_note: The printed warning also cites equations owned by another model; the audit entry keeps only this model's equations so the owner check holds.

fact_notation_claim_warnings.precise_source_claim: Figure 7 splits the purchase between a high and a low share.
fact_notation_claim_warnings.warning: The diamond prints R^i < R^i. As drawn the test never changes its answer, so the chart does not actually choose between the two shares. The skill must not describe this figure as a decision rule.

fact_notation_claim_warnings.precise_source_claim: The holding charts confirm the tabled positions.
fact_notation_claim_warnings.warning: Figure 9's bitcoin axis tops out at 0.014 while Table 6 lists the insurance holding as 1.07, and one spike is clipped by the border. Figure 17's cash path ends near 1100 against Table 6's 421.14 for the common type. Figure 18 does agree with the radical column. No chart is promoted to confirmation of the table.

fact_notation_claim_warnings.precise_source_claim: The summary, the results and the memo report one set of numbers.
fact_notation_claim_warnings.warning: The gold coefficient is 0.8592 in three places and 0.8591 in the memo. The terminal value is $132089.1078 in the summary and section 4.3 but $132089.11 in section 3.4. The missing-value fill uses past prices in the summary and the mean of the neighbouring days in section 3.1. The trader split is credited to beta, gamma, w and q in the body and to lambda in the memo. Each pair is kept; none is averaged.

fact_notation_claim_warnings.precise_source_claim: The perturbed result proves the strategy is the best.
fact_notation_claim_warnings.warning: The sentence follows a range on the authors' own result and names no other strategy. Section 4.1 also points the reader to table 8 where the adjacent table is Table 6. A bounded self-check is not a proof of optimality, and the skill must not copy the "so it is proved" wording as evidence.

gate_attestation.warning_boundary: Last pass only; no positive evidence derived from warnings.
